title: TI P4-01: read-only baseline of the live site, content and media
description:
## Goal
A read-only baseline of the live site and its content, so every later step has something to compare against. Nothing is changed anywhere.

## Context (FACT, verified 2026-10-07 read-only)
- Live: https://threat-intelligence.anth.us redirects / to /2026/july/04 (the edition page); article URLs are /2026/july/04/<slug> (18 articles linked from the edition); /newsroom answers 200; /articles, /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt are 404.
- Old backend: AppSync api jl5puwd4wnheddpkcyzzqv6pmq (auth: Cognito user pool, API key, Lambda, IAM). DynamoDB rows: Item 20 (18 published articles + 2 private editorial-doctrine items), PublishedItem 18, Edition 1, PublishedEdition 1, EditionItem 18, PublishedEditionItem 18, MediaAsset 24, PublishedMediaAsset 24, ItemTag 24, Tag 8, NewsroomSection 6, ProcedureDefinition 8, ProcedureVersion 8, ProcedureRun 25, Assignment 67, AssignmentEvent 42, Message 907, Reference 1866, ReferenceAttachment 626, ModelAttachment 585, SemanticNode 387, SemanticRelation 3258, SemanticRelationType 42, KnowledgeRawPayload 155, KnowledgeImportRun 23, KnowledgeCorpus 1. All other tables 0.
- Media bucket amplify-d3on1y5vlrxmam-ma-papyrusmediabucket0dab24-vq9lqoedok0k: 1004 objects, 254 MB: media/ 65 objects 160 MB (13 svg, 14 mp4 including two 26 MB edition-overview videos, payload md/txt), newsroom/ 530 objects 5.6 MB, corpora/ 409 objects 88 MB.
- 6 of 18 published articles have a body that differs from publications/threat_intelligence/seed/seed-edition-content.json on TI main (how-to-play-games-securely, treat-openai-accounts-like-production-infrastructure, audit-azure-blast-radius-before-attackers-do, the-balance-of-power-is-shifting, audit-aws-exposure-before-attackers-do, how-our-newsroom-learns). The live database is the authority, not the Git seed.

## Exact steps
1. In a scratch directory (not in any repo) write a script that records, for the live site: the route list (edition page, 18 article pages, /newsroom), HTTP status and redirect target per route, full HTML per route, the visible text per route, and full-page screenshots at 390, 768 and 1280 px in light and dark theme.
2. Export (read-only, SigV4 as the admin SSO session) the published models to JSON: PublishedItem, PublishedEdition, PublishedEditionItem, PublishedMediaAsset, Edition, EditionItem, Item, MediaAsset, NewsroomSection, Tag, ItemTag. Write a manifest of every S3 object under media/ (key, size, ETag).
3. Record the per-model row counts above and compare; write one SHA-256 over each exported file.
4. Record the 6 diverged articles with a unified diff of live body versus the Git seed.

## Acceptance checks
- Baseline directory contains routes, HTML, text, screenshots, model JSON, S3 manifest, checksums, and counts equal to the FACT list (or the differences are explained).
- Re-running the script a second time yields identical model JSON and S3 manifest checksums (the baseline is stable).
- Nothing in AWS or any repo was modified (git status clean; only read calls).

## Rollback
Delete the scratch directory.

## Risks
Screenshots with the animated page background need reduced-motion emulation to be comparable.

## Needs Ryan
No.

## Common rules (Phase 4 Threat Intelligence)
- Plan and facts: the assessment comment on the Phase 4 ticket (PPY-332889). Pattern: docs/migrations/pilobol-us.md and docs/standard-site.md 3.2 on origin/develop.
- Ryan: Threat Intelligence is PRE-PRODUCTION; goal is to dogfood the new backend CMS UX before converting anth.us (production). Treat as a hard cutover with brief downtime accepted unless Ryan says otherwise (open question Q1). The OLD app d3on1y5vlrxmam and its backend stay untouched and serving until the retire ticket.
- Read AGENTS.local.md first. AWS_PROFILE=legacy, us-east-1 (SSO is Ryan's). Never print env var or secret VALUES (names only). Never run ampx pipeline-deploy locally. Creating, changing or deleting AWS resources needs Ryan's explicit yes in chat for that step; deleting data or stacks is done by Ryan or on his explicit yes. Read-only AWS calls are fine.
- NEVER use /Users/home/Projects/Pilobol.us as a build dir. TI repo work: fresh clone under /Users/home/Projects/ (delete afterwards), feature branch + PR, never push to its main. Papyrus repo: worktree of origin/develop under /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-worktrees/, branch feature/PPY-<id>-<slug>, PR into develop, never merge to main, never git stash, trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>, PR body ends with the Claude Code generated-with line. In /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus (the board checkout) only run kbs; never git add or commit there.
- Gherkin first for any Papyrus behavior change (AGENTS.md). Long clear names, no line-level comments.
- Update this ticket with branch, PR link and command output when done.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Baseline captured read-only 2026-10-07. Location (outside any repo): `/Users/home/Projects/.baselines/threat-intelligence-20261007/` (`baseline/` = data, README.md = layout and re-run, 76 MB; no raw media). Counts: all 26 model counts in the FACT list match exactly (39 tables scanned, no differences, no unexpected non-empty tables); S3 media bucket manifest 1004 objects (media/ 65, newsroom/ 530, corpora/ 409; sizes match FACT); content manifest = per-row sha256 for 11 models (Item 20, PublishedItem 18, Edition 1, EditionItem 18, MediaAsset 24, ItemTag 24, Tag 8, NewsroomSection 6, Published* 1/18/24). Site: 24 routes crawled (/ 307 to /2026/july/04, edition 200, 18 articles 200, /newsroom 200, /articles /sitemap.xml /robots.txt 404); html, rendered DOM, visible text, and 120 screenshots (390/768/1280 x light/dark, reduced motion). Seed diff: exactly the 6 diverged articles named in the ticket, unified diffs in `seed-diff/`. Re-run: `./run_all.sh /path/to/new-run [--no-screenshots]` then `diff baseline/checksums.txt /path/to/new-run/checksums.txt` (needs `aws sso login --profile legacy` by Ryan; venv has playwright+boto3). Stability: a second full run gave identical checksums (models, S3 manifest, seed diffs, route manifest, text, normalized DOM). Surprises: raw article HTML differs per request (streaming order of metadata and script tags) and the animated background graph re-rolls random node/edge colors on every load even with reduced motion, so the fidelity check must compare visible text and the normalized DOM hash, not raw HTML (documented in README). Screenshots are not byte-stable, so excluded from checksums. Only GET, Scan, ListObjectsV2 and the GitHub contents read were used; no repo changes.
